subject: LexCare POC trial blueprint — models, fallbacks & success criteria
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Silver <elena.silver@lexcare.ai>
Cc: LexCare IT <it@lexcare.ai>, LexCare Procurement <procurement@lexcare.ai>
Date: Sun, 22 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: LexCare POC trial blueprint — models, fallbacks & success criteria

Hi Elena / team,

Thanks again for the call earlier — good to meet you all. Quick recap + proposed blueprint for the POC so we have a shared starting point.

Summary of what we heard
- Goal: validate a conversational triage assistant for patient intake and routing across English, Spanish, and French.
- Target metrics: >= 92% intent classification accuracy on the core 12 intents, average end-to-end latency < 400ms p50, and acceptable hallucination rate (<= 3% on the eval prompt set).
- Data: you will provide 2 weeks of anonymized historical transcripts + a 150-example hand-labeled eval set in English; localization team will add ~50 examples per locale (ES/FR).
- Infra preference: VPC deployment (not air-gapped) with isolated tenancy for PII — Redwood Private (VPC) or Dedicated are both acceptable.

POC scope & timeline (proposed)
- Week 0 (Dec 6): SOW + data sharing instructions signed; security questionnaire completed.
- Week 1–2 (Dec 13–27): data ingestion and minimal preprocessing; evaluation prompt set finalized.
- Week 3 (Jan 3–7): model staging + smoke tests.
- Week 4–5 (Jan 10–21): live trial with 2 internal routes + progressive traffic; success decision by Jan 28.

Model recommendations (initial)
- Primary (accuracy & multilingual coverage): Mistral-instruct-7B (with instruction-tuned weights) — chosen for strong instruction performance and latency at 7B.
- Fallback (robustness / long-tail recovery): Llama-2-13B (quantized Q4) — used for higher-context and cases where the primary underperforms.
- Safety & hallucination mitigation: enable response grounding + retrieval hooks in staging.

Key success criteria (proposal)
- Functional: >= 92% classification accuracy on the 12-intent set across EN/ES/FR (weighted).
- Latency: P50 < 400ms, P95 < 1s for production routes at baseline load.
- Quality: <= 3% hallucination rate on 150-sample eval set; manual review threshold defined.
- Ops: onboarding + runbook ready; rollback plan + fallback enabled.

Owners
- Sales/Commercial: Priyom (me) — SOW, pricing, stakeholder coordination.
- Runtime & deployment: Marcus Lin — staging, model pinning, routing policies.
- Success manager: Naomi Feldman — evaluation rubric, acceptance gating, user feedback loop.

Next asks for LexCare (please):
1) Confirm the above timeline and whether Jan 10 pilot start is acceptable.
2) Share anonymized transcript sample (2–3 files) and a point of contact for security/compliance.
3) Procurement: if you can confirm SOW review window + PO cadence that helps us align resources.

I attached a one-page POC charter draft (see attachments) — light doc we can update after your feedback. Happy to hop on a quick 20-min sync if useful.

Thanks,

--
Priyom Das
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
priom.das@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0192
Redwood Inference
Attachment: lexcare_poc_charter_v1.pdf (PDF, stub)
From: Elena Silver <elena.silver@lexcare.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: LexCare IT <it@lexcare.ai>, LexCare Procurement <procurement@lexcare.ai>
Date: Sun, 22 Nov 2026 19:38:00 -0800
Subject: Re: LexCare POC trial blueprint — models, fallbacks & success criteria

Thanks Priyom — really appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side:

- Timeline: Jan 10 pilot start works for us as a target. We need the SOW + security questionnaire by Dec 6 as you noted.
- Data: we'll share an anonymized sample (3 transcripts) by EOD Wed 11/25; our localization team will prioritize 50 ES/FR examples each and share the labels by Dec 20.
- Traffic estimate for pilot: expected ~300 session attempts/day, peak concurrency around 12–15 sessions — please size accordingly but this is not scale production traffic.
- Infra preference: VPC deployment is preferred; Dedicated is an option if you recommend for reliability. We are not pursuing on-prem for the pilot.
- Model choices: Mistral-instruct-7B as primary looks fine — lightweight is good. For fallback, can you confirm latency hit for Llama-2-13B (Q4) in a Dedicated pool vs Mistral baseline? We want to understand cost/latency trade-off.

Procurement: I am looping in procurement — can you attach a short pricing estimate (monthly burn for pilot configs) and a draft SOW (we need to check standard terms)?

One more operational ask: can Redwood provide a short runbook for incident response and an outline of the rollback policy (automated fallback to smaller model / static responses) so we can align stakeholders?

Happy to jump on a 20-min call Tue if helpful.

Best,
Elena

--
Elena Silver
Head of Product, LexCare
elena.silver@lexcare.ai
Attachment: none
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: LexCare POC trial blueprint — models, fallbacks & success criteria (internal)

Marcus / Naomi — forwarding the thread from LexCare. Key asks we need to cover:

- Marcus: size a Dedicated vs VPC config for the pilot (300 sessions/day, peak concurrency 15). Please include expected p50/p95 token latency for Mistral-7B and Llama-2-13B (Q4) on Dedicated GPU pool vs VPC shared. Also list estimated monthly burn for both options (pilot scope).
- Naomi: finalize eval rubric and acceptance gate for EN/ES/FR (>92% weighted accuracy + <=3% hallucination). We'll need a quick manual review plan (who samples, cadence).

For the runbook/rollback: propose we draft an automated fallback route (Mistral -> Llama-2-13B -> canned safe response) and an alerting threshold: if hallucination >4% or latency P95 > 2s for >10m then trigger rollback. Marcus, can you confirm viability?

I'll prepare a short pricing sketch for procurement to review and attach the SOW draft tomorrow.

Thanks — Priyom

--
Priyom Das

Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 11:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: LexCare POC trial blueprint — models, fallbacks & success criteria

Hi Elena / team — thanks for the quick response and the traffic details. Per your requests, attaching:
- lexcare_poc_charter_v1.pdf (light SOW + milestones)
- lexcare_eval_prompts_v1.csv (initial 150-sample eval set, English + placeholders for ES/FR)

Short answers inline to your questions:
- Latency tradeoff: Mistral-instruct-7B p50 ~ 180–240ms on a small Dedicated instance profile (A100-class), p95 ~ 650–800ms depending on batching. Llama-2-13B (Q4) p50 ~ 320–420ms, p95 ~ 1.0–1.6s on the same pool. Expect a cost delta ~ 30–40% higher for 13B vs 7B for equivalent throughput. We'll attach a simple table in the SOW PDF.
- Dedicated vs VPC: for the pilot we recommend VPC with reserved capacity (Dedicated) if you want consistent latency and simplified fallbacks. If budget is tight, VPC shared with pinning to warm instances is possible but carries some variance.
- Runbook & rollback: Marcus will own the runbook. Proposed automated fallback chain: Mistral-7B -> Llama-2-13B (Q4) -> static safe reply + ops page. Alerting thresholds documented in the attachment.

Next steps (action items)
1) LexCare: confirm acceptance of the Jan 10 pilot start and provide the anonymized transcripts by 11/25.
2) LexCare Procurement: review attached SOW and send back any redlines; Priyom will follow up with formal pricing.
3) Marcus: I'll ask you to produce the Dedicated sizing + cost table by EOD Wed (11/25).
4) Naomi: please prepare the evaluation plan and sampling cadence; share by Thur (11/26).

If that all looks good I'll schedule a 20-min kickoff for Mon Jan 10 and circulate calendar invites.

Thanks everyone — looking forward to moving this forward.

--
Priyom Das
